input.quote: 2.2 Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
input.rationale: Section 2.2 imposes a sole-supplier obligation on Customer for hosted analytics services for the entire term, with no category narrowing, no 12-month limit, and no performance-based exit — that is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback. It also contradicts Section 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and Section 12.3 (Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity commitment), so deleting the exclusivity restores internal consistency. Redline converts Vendor to a non-exclusive provider (preferred position); a narrow 12-month category exclusivity with automatic termination on SLA or delivery failure is offered as a fallback in the comment.

ops.oldText: Vendor will be Customer's sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services throughout the term.
ops.newText: Vendor will be a non-exclusive provider of hosted analytics services to Customer, and Customer may obtain the same or similar services from any third party.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a sole-supplier commitment, so we have made Vendor a non-exclusive provider consistent with our right under Sections 2.1 and 12.3 to source freely. If exclusivity is commercially important, we could discuss a narrow 12-month category exclusivity that ends automatically on any service level or delivery failure.
proposal.summary: Convert Vendor's sole and exclusive provider status into a non-exclusive appointment.
